title: Images with Captions and Sources knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which goal is most directly related to “Images with Captions and Sources”?
options: It helps an author explain the purpose of images with captions and sources in a browser document.
Change the visual design without changing page structure
Store trusted application data directly in the browser markup
Replace testing with assumptions based on appearance
questions.answer_key: It helps an author explain the purpose of images with captions and sources in a browser document.
questions.explanation: This lesson focuses on images with captions and sources. Figure groups self-contained media or illustrative content that is referenced from the main flow.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with images with captions and sources?
options: Choose the native HTML meaning, check paths and constraints, and verify the result.
Use elements only for their default visual appearance
Assume the browser will always repair mistakes correctly
Skip accessibility checks when the page looks readable
questions.answer_key: Choose the native HTML meaning, check paths and constraints, and verify the result.
questions.explanation: Semantic markup and repeatable checks make pages more understandable and easier to maintain.

questions.prompt: Which check provides the strongest evidence that an HTML example is ready to keep?
options: Inspect the source, test the browser behavior, and use a relevant validator or manual checklist.
Confirm that one screenshot looks acceptable
Open the file once and assume all states work
Add more markup until the warning disappears
questions.answer_key: Inspect the source, test the browser behavior, and use a relevant validator or manual checklist.
questions.explanation: Visual review, source/DOM inspection, and the relevant validation or accessibility check complement one another.
